forks.question: For configured Python and TypeScript, how narrow is the touched code's test scope? For example, if one part contains src/orders/, src/billing/, tests/orders/ and tests/billing/, and the plan names only src/orders/service.py, may the builder also add tests/billing/test_refund.py? The captured repository contract currently identifies parts and commands, but has no source-to-test-area associations. Both options implement all of #654 in one plumbing pull request, including staging, execution, copy-back, repairs, merge-base CI scope, documentation and the existing protections.

options.says: Use the captured part as the Python or TypeScript test scope: touching its source permits new framework-conventional test files throughout that part, including both test areas in the example, provided captured test discovery includes them; tests belonging to other parts, existing unnamed files, production and test configuration remain protected, and Go keeps its precise package and embedded-asset ownership.

Keep Python and TypeScript regression additions within the touched source area and its associated test area, so tests/billing/test_refund.py is refused in the example; capture explicit source-to-test-area associations in repository policy for separate test trees, require files without an established association to be named in the plan, retain framework-conventional filenames and all existing protections, and keep Go's precise package and embedded-asset ownership.

usage.summary: Wrote [proposal.json](proposal.json) with one fork: whether regression tests may span the touched part or only its associated source/test area. The check tool confirmed no validation is needed for this question-only proposal; `repo/` remains unchanged.
